page: Amazon Web Services r5b.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8259CL processor operating at 3.1 GHz, delivering 32 vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU supports AVX-512 extensions including AVX-512 F and AVX-512 VNNI, alongside hardware acceleration for AES encryption and BMI2 operations. Cache resources comprise 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a shared 35 MB L3 cache.

Hardware allocations center around memory density, providing 256.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, which equates to an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio (8.0 GB per vCPU). The instance does not feature onboard GPUs or bundled local instance storage, relying instead on network-attached storage via AWS services. Networking throughput is defined by a 10 Gbps baseline bandwidth connection.

Benchmark measurements establish consistent middle-tier performance across multi-threaded operations and memory tests. The instance recorded a multi-core Geekbench score of 10,096.0, a PassMark CPU score of 25,455.23, and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression throughput of 65.55 GB/sec. Large-block memory tests yielded 84.32 GB/sec read and 45.02 GB/sec write bandwidth, supporting 26.41 million Redis SET operations per second and 10,429.82 on the PassMark database operations benchmark. Single-thread processing registers lower in comparative rankings, evidenced by a stress-ng single-core score of 1,286.09 and single-threaded gzip compression at 22.6 GB/sec.

Cost efficiency is tied directly to the large DDR4 memory allocation and dedicated vCPU scale. The absence of integrated local NVMe storage and dedicated accelerators means that infrastructure expenditure is focused on system RAM capacity and multi-core throughput. These specifications make the r5b.8xlarge fit for large in-memory key-value stores, distributed database caches, transactional databases, and memory-bound ETL processing pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services r5b.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It is configured with an Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processor clocked at 3.1 GHz, providing 32 vCPUs across 16 dedicated physical cores with AVX-512 vector support. The instance includes 256.0 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. It provides a 10 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, contains no bundled local storage, and includes no discrete GPU hardware. Benchmark results display average multi-core and memory throughput, reaching 26.41 million Redis SET operations per second, alongside 84.32 GB/sec uncached large-block memory read bandwidth, while single-core compute performance measures in the lower quartile. This instance configuration is primarily fit for in-memory caching systems, distributed relational or NoSQL database workloads, and large enterprise memory-intensive data processing pipelines.
